title: Meta's Muse Spark Open: What You Need to Know About the New Open-Weight AI Model
excerpt: Meta has launched Muse Spark Open, an 816 billion parameter open-weight AI model designed for Macs and complex developer tasks.
metaDescription: Discover Meta's Muse Spark Open, an 816 billion parameter open-weight AI model designed to run on Macs and handle complex coding and agentic tasks.
content:
Meta just launched what it calls the most capable open-weight AI model in the US, according to TechCrunch. It's called **Muse Spark Open**. What makes it stand out is simple: it's built to run on Apple hardware while packing serious multimodal and agentic features. If you're building software or managing an engineering team, this bridges the gap between running local models and scaling up in the cloud. Following recent drops like [Meta's Muse Wonder Is Here: What's New and What It Means for Developers](/blog/metas-muse-wonder-frontier-model-announcement), this gives you another option for your local and cloud setups.

## What was announced — the key facts, clearly

Meta's new release drops some heavy specs into the open-weight space. Their benchmark scores put it ahead of most competing open models.

* **Massive Scale:** It runs on **816 billion parameters** for deep reasoning tasks.
* **Context Window:** You get a **1 million token context window**, which means you can dump entire codebases or massive PDFs straight into it.
* **Multimodal Architecture:** It handles text, code, and vision natively.
* **Hardware Focus:** It's tuned specifically for high-end Apple hardware, with API options available too.

## What's new — what changed or how it compares

Most frontier models force you into the cloud. Muse Spark Open takes a different route, pairing deep hardware optimization with agentic capabilities. Meta tied it directly to Muse Code, their AI terminal, showing it can handle automated dev loops.

* **Local Mac Execution:** You can run it directly on Apple machines, though you'll need the right specs.
* **Agentic Workflows:** Meta tested it on a Mastodon client, letting the model write features, fix bugs, and build the app on its own.
* **Video Processing:** They ran it inside DaVinci Resolve, where it reviewed and cropped video footage directly.
* **Industry Advantages:** Open-weight gives you control, transparency, and lower long-term costs compared to closed APIs.

## What it means for businesses and developers — practical impact

Open-weight models make it easier to build custom AI infrastructure. But don't expect to spin this up on a standard laptop. Running Muse Spark Open locally takes serious hardware.

* **High Hardware Demands:** You need at least **1 terabyte of RAM** to run it locally, and it shines on a Mac Studio with an **M5 Ultra chip**.
* **Coding Workhorse:** If you have the memory for it, you get a local engine that handles desktop tasks and complex coding without sending data to a third party.
* **API Accessibility:** Don't have a Mac Studio cluster? You can still call the model via standard API platforms.

## How to try it or prepare — concrete next steps

Evaluating an 816-billion-parameter model takes planning. Look at your current setup and figure out if local execution makes sense for your security needs or if you should stick to APIs.

* **Audit Your Infrastructure:** Check your hardware against that 1 terabyte RAM threshold before buying a Mac Studio with an M5 Ultra chip.
* **Explore API Options:** Test the model via available APIs first to check its output before spending money on local hardware.
* **Test Agentic Use Cases:** Run pilot projects on automated bug fixes, refactoring tasks, or heavy media processing.

## The takeaway

Meta's **Muse Spark Open** is a major addition to the open-weight ecosystem, combining 816 billion parameters with local Mac support and API access. Running it locally takes heavy-duty hardware like a Mac Studio with an M5 Ultra chip and 1 terabyte of RAM, but the transparency, flexibility, and agentic power make it worth looking at for your next project.
